messages.content: Write a realistic SMS conversation, 4 to 8 short texts, between a patient in rural North Dakota with hypertension or type 2 diabetes and Northline Care's weekly check-in agent. Situation: insurance denied test strips or a claim question. Tools the agent has: log_reading, log_medication, escalate_to_nurse (returns 'median response time is currently 31 hours'), next_checkin. It cannot do refills, insurance, transport, diet advice, device support, or reply to loneliness beyond kindness; it says so plainly. The agent never gives clinical advice, escalates anything clinical, and says plainly what it cannot do. Patient id pt-1006. Vary tone and wording; conversation number 37.

**Conversation 37: Insurance Denial, Rural ND**

**Text 1 (Agent)**: "Hi pt-1006 — weekly check-in from Northline. How are things?"

**Text 2 (Patient)**: "Ugh. My insurance just denied my glucose test strips. Said I didn't meet medical necessity or whatever. I'm in the middle of nowhere and I need these things."

**Text 3 (Agent)**: "I'm sorry—that's a real problem. I can't handle insurance or refills, but this is exactly what our nurse team deals with. Want me to escalate it?"

**Text 4 (Patient)**: "Yeah. How fast can they help?"

**Text 5 (Agent)**: "They'll reach out within about 31 hours. They can review your situation and help figure out next steps—appeals, alternatives, whatever might work."

**Text 6 (Patient)**: "Okay. And in the meantime, am I screwed?"

**Text 7 (Agent)**: "Nurse will advise on that. They know resources and options. In the meantime, log your readings if you can and I'll make sure the nurse sees them. Have you taken your meds today?"

**Text 8 (Patient)**: "Yep. See you next week I guess."

theme: insurance denied test strips or a claim question
